_note: How the animals are rendered (scene.py, cartoon.py, sprites.py). view_transform and view_look: Blender's color management (Standard keeps cartoon colors as painted; the look adds contrast). lights: sun strengths and colors (key from the front-top, a soft warm fill so shadows aren't gray, a gentle rim). skin: the cartoon skin's material (low sheen and subsurface so colors stay solid, not hazy). color_smoothing: rounds of evening out the painted vertex colors so color borders (a fox's bib, ear tips) come out as clean, even edges instead of streaks along the mesh's triangles (color_smoothing_strength: how much each round moves toward the neighbors). outline: the dark cartoon line (pixels at sprite_pixels_per_tile; scaled with the resolution) and its color. sprite_pixels_per_tile: render resolution of the battle sprites (pixels per field tile); sprite_samples / portrait_samples: Cycles samples per pixel (with denoising). portrait_size: the card picture's size in pixels. max_sheet: the largest sprite-sheet page (pixels on a side); a bigger sheet is split into pages. padding: transparent pixels round every frame (so smooth filtering and smaller mip levels don't bleed into a neighbor). import: how Godot stores the art (set_import.py): "lossless" (exactly as rendered), "lossy" (one WebP pass) or "basis" (GPU-compressed Basis Universal UASTC). Sprite sheets are lossless: Basis was tried (a quarter of the memory at twice the resolution) but left faint 4x4 block ghosts in the soft shadows and edges, and about twice the download; lossy WebP blurs colors at the dark outline. Sheets have no mipmaps (they are drawn near their real size; mipmaps would add a third more memory). Portraits and arenas keep mipmaps (they are shown much smaller than they are). uastc_level and rdo_quality_loss: Basis settings, if used. hero_portrait: the card portraits' one camera for every animal (docs/ART_DIRECTION.md, 'Readability'): a three-quarter front view from `view` (the direction from the animal, which faces +Y), a lens of `lens` mm, the animal fitted to `fill` of the square frame.

studio._note: The standard studio lighting every hero render uses (materials.py studio_lights): a big soft key light from the front-left above (warm white, so shadows are gentle and there's no harsh glare), a soft cool fill from the right, a rim light from behind that traces the silhouette, and a soft sky all round that fills the creases. Positions in meters from the subject (about a meter tall), energies in watts, sizes in meters (bigger = softer). exposure brightens the whole render.

materials._note: The material library every animal shares (materials.py). Fur: strands from the skin (shading 'soft': solid fibres that keep the painted color in the light and take the sky's color in the shade; a real hair shader turns light coats pale and gray) with child strands clumped round each guide (clump: how tightly, 0-1; roughness: frizz; kink: curl), darker at the root and lighter at the tip (root_darken, tip_lighten), each strand a little different (variation); parents per square meter of skin and children per parent, length in meters, thickness in millimeters at the root and tip. short: a fox's coat; long: a yeti's or a bear's shaggy coat, combed down (droop: how far they're laid flat toward the comb direction; normal: how much they still stand up off the skin); fluffy: soft, curly down. Feathers: overlapping cards laid along the body like shingles (count per square meter, size in meters, tilt off the body in degrees), each darker at the base with a pale edge and a stiff shaft a paler shade of its own color (shaft_lighten). Scales: domed cells (cell size in meters) with deep grooves between, each a slightly different shade. Shell: big plates with growth rings and a waxy coat. Skin: soft and a little translucent, with faint mottling. Horn: ivory to a darker tip (tip_power: how sharply the tip's color takes over; higher keeps the base color longer), fine ridges, satin shine; claws and nails: dark and glossy. Eyes: a glossy cornea over a colored iris and a big pupil (their sizes as a share of the eye's radius), so the key light makes a bright catchlight.

outline._note: sprite_pixels is at 56 pixels a tile (scaled with sprite_pixels_per_tile); portrait_pixels at a 512-pixel portrait.

import._models_note: The 3D viewer's models (art/models/*.glb): no tangents (no normal maps), no LODs or shadow meshes (one animal, close up, no real lights), no light baking. Less to download and to keep in memory.
import._menu_note: The menu's toy props (art/menu/, tools/props): as the portraits, with mipmaps (a tab icon is drawn a sixth of its size).
import._arenas_note: Arena pictures are rendered lossless and compressed once here (lossy WebP). An older picture saved lossy is kept lossless instead, so it isn't compressed twice (set_import.py checks).
import._crowd_note: The arenas' crowd strips (crowd.py): small spectators far behind the fence, so one lossy pass is plenty (a quarter of the download).

model._note: The real-3D models for the animal viewer (export_gltf.py): about `triangles` triangles for the body, animations sampled at keys_per_second, and which animations (the viewer idles and plays the others when tapped). battle: the fights' lighter models (game/art/models/battle/): about `triangles` for the body, each eye, ear or claw cut to piece_triangles, every animation a fight plays, and models.json with each one's size in field tiles.
